climate.overview_html: With COP31 opening in Antalya eleven days away, the final pre-summit week produced Türkiye’s Antalya Artificial Intelligence Pledge — the full text of which was released October 28, calling on governments and companies to mandate clean-power procurement for AI data centres and require energy-use disclosure — even as UN climate chief Simon Stiell warned Big Tech is “on thin ice” because data-centre growth is simultaneously fuelling fossil-fuel demand. An Urgewald analysis published October 27 confirmed that both COP31 co-hosts — Türkiye and Australia — are still actively expanding coal, even as the COP31 presidency’s agenda mentions neither coal, oil nor gas for phase-out. Against that backdrop, Copernicus ERA5 data confirmed August 2026 as the hottest month ever recorded in the modern instrumental era at 1.65°C above the pre-industrial average, and October is now tracking toward its own warmest-on-record mark as the strengthening El Niño drives Niño 3.4 sea-surface temperatures to all-time highs.

items.source: BusinessGreen / Japan Times / Sustain&Play / Beyond Fossil Fuels
items.headline: COP31 Presidency Releases Full Text of Antalya AI Pledge: Data-Centre Disclosure, Clean-Power Mandates, Global Progress Tracking — UN Chief Warns Big Tech “On Thin Ice” as Data Centres Boost Fossil Demand
items.summary: Türkiye's COP31 Presidency released the full text of the proposed Antalya Artificial Intelligence Pledge on October 28, seeking sign-on from governments, NGOs and businesses. The pledge commits signatories to requiring AI providers to disclose data-centre energy and environmental impact, mandate procurement of clean power for AI workloads, and establish a global collective-progress tracking process. EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra said the EU was weighing whether to sign, calling it to have 'interesting characteristics'; the US is not participating in the COP process. Critics, including Beyond Fossil Fuels, say the pledge provides no credible evidence AI delivers net climate benefits. WRI's Evan Tachovsky said it sets the right direction but lacks accountability mechanisms. UN climate chief Simon Stiell separately warned Big Tech is 'on thin ice' because AI data centres are simultaneously boosting fossil-fuel demand. The pledge is scheduled for discussion on November 10, a dedicated technology and AI day at the Antalya summit.

items.headline: Urgewald: Both COP31 Hosts Expanding Coal — Türkiye and Australia Building New Capacity Ahead of Summit; Presidency Agenda Names Neither Coal, Oil nor Gas; Koç Holding Fossil Ties Draw Sponsor Criticism
items.summary: An Urgewald coal-tracking analysis, reported October 27, confirms that COP31 co-hosts Türkiye and Australia are both actively pursuing coal expansion — developing new mines, export capacity and power plants — even as the COP31 presidency's published agenda names neither coal, oil nor gas for phase-out. Climate Change News separately reports that Koç Holding, a major Turkish COP31 corporate partner, owns oil refiner Tüpraş, which is running at full capacity, and that Koç's stated climate targets have slipped. Campaigners including Amnesty International are calling for limits on fossil-fuel lobbying access at the Antalya summit, which runs November 9–20.

items.headline: Copernicus ERA5: August 2026 Was Hottest Month on Instrumental Record at 1.65°C Above Pre-Industrial; Global Ocean Hit 21.1°C Record; October Now Tracking Warmest on Record; El Niño Niño 3.4 SST at All-Time High
items.summary: Climate Central's September 2026 briefing, drawing on Copernicus ERA5 and Copernicus Marine Service data, confirmed that August 2026 was the hottest month ever recorded in the modern instrumental climate record at 1.65°C above the 1850–1900 pre-industrial average, surpassing the previous record from July 2023. The global average sea surface temperature for extra-polar oceans hit 21.1°C on 22 August — also a new record. August was the 11th consecutive month globally above the 1.5°C Paris threshold. Celsius.earth's probabilistic projection now places October 2026 on track to become the warmest October in the ERA5 dataset by approximately 0.23°C over October 2023, driven by the strengthening El Niño whose Niño 3.4 index set an all-time record high for SST in early October.

items.headline: UN: Global Warming Will Breach 1.5°C Within Years; Scientific Consensus Ahead of COP31 Holds Temporary Overshoot Now Inevitable; Deep Cuts Could Limit Duration and Peak
items.summary: A UN News synthesis confirms that the scientific consensus ahead of COP31 is that the 1.5°C threshold will be breached in the near term. UNEP's Emissions Gap Report 2026 'The Point of Return' (October 21) and the WMO Greenhouse Gas Bulletin No. 22 (October 27) together establish that keeping below 1.5°C without any overshoot is no longer possible, but that deep emissions cuts could limit the duration and severity of the overshoot, potentially returning temperatures toward 1.5°C later this century. Current policies place warming at 2.8°C; even full NDC delivery would yield 2.6°C. CO₂ concentration reached 426.8 ppm in 2025, the highest in at least 800,000 years of ice-core records.

major_events.name: Super Typhoon In-fa (JTWC 30W) — Upgraded to Super Typhoon 28 Oct; 150 mph Sustained, Peak ~155 mph Thursday; Typhoon Condition III Agrihan, Pagan & Alamagan CNMI; Direct Hit Northern Islands ~Friday 30 Oct Evening
major_events.status: As of 28–29 Oct: JTWC upgraded In-fa to super typhoon status late October 28 with maximum sustained winds of 150 mph (130 kt); JTWC’s forecast places a peak near 155 mph on Thursday before gradual weakening ahead of landfall in the northern CNMI. CNMI Governor David Apatang declared Typhoon Condition III — destructive winds of 74 mph or greater possible within 48 hours — for Agrihan, Pagan and Alamagan; residents are urged to shelter from Friday morning until sunrise Saturday. RNZ confirms a typhoon warning is in effect for the northern CNMI. Saipan, Tinian and Rota are not under a typhoon watch but will experience heavy rain and dangerous building seas from Thursday night onward.
major_events.impact: Agrihan/Pagan/Alamagan (CNMI): Typhoon Condition III; direct hit forecast ~Fri Oct 30 evening at Cat 4–5 (peak ~155 mph); shelter in place from Fri morning to Sat sunrise. Saipan/Tinian/Rota: heavy rain bands, dangerous surf, no watch. Guam: outside cone, monitoring. Large dangerous swells building across Marianas.

major_events.name: Southeast Asian Peatland Haze (Indonesia / Borneo / Sumatra) — Rain Brings Surface Relief; Haze Easing over Singapore & KL; Wet Season Transition Expected Late October; Underground Fires Persist; 333,470+ Respiratory Cases
major_events.status: As of 27–29 Oct: Rain reached fire-affected provinces on October 27, reducing visible smoke plumes over southern Sumatra and Kalimantan by satellite, Al Jazeera reports. The National News reports the transboundary haze has begun to subside over Singapore and Kuala Lumpur, but underground peat — smouldering in columns up to 8 metres below the surface — cannot be reached by aerial water-bombing or extinguished by surface rainfall; 61 aircraft remain deployed. BMKG forecasts the wet season transition in East Kalimantan to begin in the final days of October. Cumulative toll: 333,470+ confirmed acute respiratory illness cases across seven provinces; WMO has described this as potentially the worst transboundary haze event on record in Southeast Asia. Indonesia and Malaysia have closed hundreds of schools; protests demanding a national disaster declaration continue in Jakarta.
major_events.impact: Indonesia: 333,470+ respiratory cases (7 provinces); ~1.9M ha burned; 61 aircraft deployed; underground fires unresponsive to rain; wet season onset expected late Oct/early Nov. Malaysia/Singapore/Philippines: haze subsiding. ~40M people exposed region-wide.

weather.overview_html: Super Typhoon In-fa intensified to 150 mph on October 28 and is tracking toward the northern CNMI, with a direct hit on Pagan and Agrihan forecast for Friday October 30 — Typhoon Condition III is in effect for the northern islands. In the Bay of Bengal, Cyclone Arnab completed its life cycle after making landfall near Bapatla–Machilipatnam, Andhra Pradesh on October 28, killing at least 2 people and displacing 570,000; the system is now dissipating inland. Southeast Asia’s peatland haze crisis shows its first signs of improvement as rain reached Sumatra and Kalimantan on October 27, though 333,470 respiratory cases have been confirmed across Indonesia and underground fires continue to burn. Globally, October 2026 is on track to become the warmest October in the instrumental record as the El Niño strengthens.

items.headline: Cyclone Arnab Post-Landfall Wrap: System Dissipating After Bapatla–Machilipatnam Landfall; 2 Dead, 570,000 Evacuated, Kakinada Waterlogged, Power Infrastructure Downed Across East Godavari — Residual Rain Moving into Odisha & Jharkhand
items.summary: Cyclone Arnab made landfall near Bapatla–Machilipatnam, Andhra Pradesh at approximately 1:20 a.m. IST on October 28, with sustained winds of 125–135 km/h and gusts to 150 km/h. The system has since moved inland and is weakening rapidly, expected to fully dissipate within 24 hours. Final confirmed impact: at least 2 deaths by electrocution, widespread tree and power-pole damage across Kakinada, East Godavari and Machilipatnam districts, and waterlogging throughout Kakinada town. 570,000 residents had been pre-emptively evacuated. School closures in Jharkhand and Odisha were extended through October 29. Residual heavy rainfall is tracking northwest toward Odisha and Jharkhand. The IMD considers the cyclone threat ended.

items.headline: Tropical Storm Vance Persists in Eastern Pacific ~200 km WSW of Cabo Corrientes, Mexico; NHC Continues Advisories; Weakening Forecast; Atlantic Basin Quiet
items.summary: Tropical Storm Vance was persisting in the eastern Pacific approximately 200 km west-southwest of Cabo Corrientes, Mexico, as of October 28, with the NHC continuing regular advisories at approximately 30 knots. A gradual weakening trend is forecast as the system drifts over cooler waters. No threat to the US mainland or major population centres is anticipated. The Atlantic basin remains quiet with no active tropical cyclones and no new development expected in the next seven days.

items.headline: October 2026 Tracking as Warmest October on Record at ~+0.23°C vs. October 2023; El Niño Niño 3.4 SST Sets All-Time Record; Many US Stations in Top-5 Warmest Octobers
items.summary: Celsius.earth's probabilistic projection as of late October gives high confidence that October 2026 will set a new record as the warmest October in the ERA5 and instrumental record, approximately 0.23°C above October 2023. Multiple US observation stations including Wausau, Wisconsin, are tracking in their top five warmest Octobers in over a century of records. The exceptional warmth is driven by a strengthening El Niño whose Niño 3.4 index set a new all-time record high for sea-surface temperature in early October, per Climate Central reporting. The all-time warmest single month in any calendar month remains August 2026 at 1.65°C above pre-industrial.

renewables.overview_html: Clean energy capital continues to flow at elevated levels: BloombergNEF’s first-half 2026 data shows global clean-energy investment at US$327.5 billion, with co-located solar-plus-storage surging to a record US$25 billion — nearly double the prior six months — and US solar hitting a record US$45.8 billion (+41% year-on-year). Australia broke its annual large-scale solar investment record at 3.5 GWp of final investment decisions, while Masdar raised US$600 million via a blue bond on the London Stock Exchange on October 27, part of a US$6 billion European expansion push into offshore wind and green hydrogen.

items.headline: BloombergNEF H1 2026 Clean Energy: US$327.5 B Global Investment (Flat HoH, −21% from H2 2024 Peak); US Solar +41% YoY to Record US$45.8 B; US Wind Doubled to US$13.8 B; Co-Located Solar+Storage Hits Record US$25 B
items.summary: BloombergNEF's first-half 2026 clean energy investment data shows $327.5 billion globally, broadly flat versus the prior six months but 21% below the H2 2024 record peak. The standout subsector is co-located solar and storage, which attracted a record $25 billion, nearly double H2 2025. US solar investment rose 41% year-on-year to a record $45.8 billion, and US wind investment more than doubled to $13.8 billion. Clean energy capital spending is reported to outpace fossil fuel investment globally by close to two to one. Hardware cost declines continue to compress per-MW metrics even as deployed capacity grows.

items.source: PV Tech / Australian Clean Energy Regulator
items.headline: Australia Solar Sets Annual FID Record: 3.5 GWp Large-Scale in 2026; Total Renewable FIDs Reach 5 GW, Above Full-Year 2025 Record; Renewables Generated More Electricity Than Fossil Fuels Last Month
items.summary: Australia's Clean Energy Regulator data, reported October 16, shows large-scale solar projects at 3.5 GWp of final investment decisions in 2026 — a new annual record. Total large-scale renewable investment decisions reached 5 GW this year, exceeding the previous full-year record of 4.9 GW. Energy Minister Chris Bowen stated that renewable energy generated more electricity in Australia's national grid than fossil fuels in the preceding month — a first. The surge is driven by state auction programs and improving project economics across New South Wales, Victoria and Queensland.

items.headline: Masdar Raises US$600 M via Five-Year Blue Bond on London Stock Exchange; Part of US$6 B Debt Plan for European Offshore Wind, Solar & Green Hydrogen Expansion
items.summary: Abu Dhabi's Masdar issued a $600 million five-year blue bond on the London Stock Exchange on October 27, the latest tranche in a $6 billion debt-raising plan. Proceeds are earmarked for offshore wind in the UK, Germany and Greece, as well as solar and green hydrogen projects. Masdar — jointly owned by ADNOC, Mubadala and TAQA — targets 100 GW of renewable energy capacity globally by 2030. The bond was reportedly oversubscribed. Blue bonds are debt instruments linked to sustainable ocean or water-related development.

items.headline: Cubico Gets UK Development Consent for 147 MW Frodsham Solar with Battery Storage (Cheshire); Statkraft Signs 10-Year Hybrid PPA with Deutsche Bahn’s DB Energie for 107 MW Brandenburg Solar
items.summary: Two notable European renewable deals were announced around October 27. Cubico Sustainable Investments received UK development consent for its 147 MW Frodsham Solar project in Cheshire, which includes co-located battery storage — one of the larger solar approvals in England this year. Separately, Statkraft signed a 10-year hybrid power purchase agreement with DB Energie, Deutsche Bahn's electricity unit, for a 107 MW solar farm in Brandenburg, Germany. The hybrid PPA combines fixed and variable price components. Greenvolt is also installing approximately 25 MWp of solar carports across Carrefour retail sites in France.

items.headline: NLC India Renewables Wins 300 MW Grid-Connected Wind Project in Gujarat Through Competitive State Bidding; Company Diversifying Away from Legacy Coal Business
items.summary: NLC India Renewables Limited, a subsidiary of state-owned lignite and coal company NLC India, secured a 300 MW grid-connected wind power project in Gujarat through a competitive state bidding round, announced October 29. The award adds to NLC India's growing renewables pipeline as it diversifies from legacy coal operations. Gujarat is one of India's top wind states by installed capacity, with several GW of active tender pipeline from GUVNL and SECI procurement programs.

items.headline: Peak Energy Closes US$108 M Series B for Sodium-Ion Battery Expansion; Led by General Motors Ventures, LG Technology Ventures & Eclipse; Targets Cost-Competitive Stationary Grid Storage
items.summary: US sodium-ion battery developer Peak Energy closed a $108 million Series B round led by General Motors Ventures alongside LG Technology Ventures and Eclipse, reported around October 21. Sodium-ion chemistry eliminates lithium, cobalt and nickel, using lower-cost and more geographically diversified materials. The technology targets stationary grid storage as a cost-competitive alternative to lithium iron phosphate batteries. The GM Ventures participation signals automotive OEM interest in non-lithium battery supply chains for grid applications. Peak Energy plans to use proceeds for US manufacturing scale-up.

science.overview_html: The week’s highest-impact paper is a Nature study from Microsoft Research and MIT showing that their open-source Probabilistic Bias Correction (PBC) layer roughly doubled the skill of ECMWF’s subseasonal AI model for the critical two-to-six-week window — the range where classical models lose predictive power fastest. A companion preprint, arXiv:2610.25545, directly challenges whether probabilistic AI weather models remain reliable deep in the tail of their training distribution — finding skill degrades faster than the models themselves indicate, with major implications for risk applications. Meanwhile, Copernicus ERA5 confirmed August 2026 as the hottest month in the instrumental record at 1.65°C, providing the climate backdrop against which all of these forecasting advances are measured.

items.headline: Microsoft–MIT Probabilistic Bias Correction (PBC) Doubles ECMWF Subseasonal AI Skill for 2–6 Week Window; Tripled Positive Precipitation Skill; Open Source; Kenya Met Seeks Deployment for Monsoon Forecasts
items.meta: Judah Cohen, Lester Mackey, Hannah Guan, Soukayna Mouatadid et al. · Nature, Oct 2026
items.summary: A Microsoft Research and MIT team published a Nature paper on October 14 introducing Probabilistic Bias Correction (PBC), a machine-learning post-processing layer that sits on top of existing forecast systems — rather than replacing them — to remove systematic biases in the two-to-six-week (subseasonal) forecast range. Applied to ECMWF's dynamical ensemble over 2016–2024, PBC tripled the raw model's positive precipitation skill score (from RPSS 0.023) and converted previously negative-skill temperature and pressure forecasts into skilful predictions. Applied to ECMWF's subseasonal AI model, PBC roughly doubled overall skill. The method is low-cost, runs quickly on standard hardware, and has been fully open-sourced. Kenya's national meteorological office contacted the team about deploying PBC for monsoon rainfall forecasts, illustrating rapid-adoption potential in NWP-constrained settings.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.25545 — “Beyond the Record: Evaluating Probabilistic AI Weather Forecasts Deep in the Tail” — AIWP Models Overconfident on Extreme Events Outside Training Distribution
items.summary: A preprint posted October 18 to cs.LG examines whether probabilistic AI weather prediction (AIWP) models maintain calibration and skill when applied to extreme events that lie deep in the tail of their training distribution — events beyond anything the model has seen during training. The authors build a systematic evaluation framework using ERA5 reanalysis and station observations, testing several probabilistic AIWP models. Results find that forecast skill degrades in the far tail faster than the models' own uncertainty estimates imply: the models are overconfident for low-probability, high-impact weather regimes. The findings have direct implications for using AIWP outputs in flood forecasting, wildfire risk, catastrophe modeling and financial weather-risk applications.

items.headline: Colorado State University Develops AI Hail Prediction System Targeting Hours-to-Days Lead Times Across Colorado & Wyoming — vs. Current <30-Minute Window; Could Transform Ag Insurance & Grid Risk
items.summary: Colorado State University researchers are developing an AI-based hail forecasting system capable of issuing probabilistic hail-threat predictions hours or even days in advance — a dramatic improvement over the current operational window of under 30 minutes from radar detection to public warning. The system targets Colorado and Wyoming, states with heavy agricultural and infrastructure hail exposure. The team is training models on historical radar, sounding, and verification data to identify atmospheric environments conducive to large hail well before convective initiation. If operational, such a system could fundamentally change how agricultural insurers, grid operators and emergency managers prepare for hail events, which cause several billion dollars in US economic losses annually.

items.headline: Climate Central September 2026 Briefing: August 2026 Hottest Month in ERA5 Record at 1.65°C; Global SST Hit Record 21.1°C; 11th Consecutive Month Above 1.5°C; El Niño SST Hits All-Time High
items.summary: Climate Central's September 2026 briefing, drawing on Copernicus ERA5 and Copernicus Marine Service data, confirmed that August 2026 was the hottest month ever recorded in the modern instrumental climate record at 1.65°C above the 1850–1900 pre-industrial average, surpassing the previous record set in July 2023. Global average sea surface temperature for extra-polar oceans reached a new record high of 21.1°C on 22 August. August was the 11th consecutive month in which the global monthly average exceeded the 1.5°C Paris threshold. The WMO confirmed El Niño onset in June 2026; Niño 3.4 SST set an all-time record high in early October, raising the prospect that 2026 could surpass 2023 as the hottest calendar year in the instrumental record.

items.headline: COP31 AI-Climate Tension: Data Centres Drive Fossil Demand While AI Claims Climate Benefits; No Measurement Framework for Net Impact; UN Climate Chief Warns Big Tech; WRI Flags Accountability Gap
items.summary: A Beyond Fossil Fuels analysis published October 28 directly challenges the Antalya AI Pledge's core premise, arguing no credible evidence base supports claims that AI delivers net climate benefits. The analysis notes that IEA projections show data-centre electricity demand is growing 26–36% per year, and is causing utilities in several US states to extend fossil-fuel plant operations and revive retired coal capacity. UN climate chief Simon Stiell warned Big Tech it is 'on thin ice', saying data centre growth is undermining the emissions reductions AI tools elsewhere claim to enable. WRI's Evan Tachovsky notes a fundamental measurement problem: no standardised framework exists for quantifying the net climate impact of AI applications against their energy footprint — a research gap the pledge does not address.

items.title: Vaisala Completes Acquisition of AI Weather Company Atmo, Inc. (US$70 M Fixed + Up to US$60 M Earn-Out)
items.body_html: Finnish measurement and environmental technology company Vaisala completed its acquisition of San Francisco AI weather startup Atmo, Inc. on October 28, closing a deal first announced June 17. The fixed purchase price was USD 70 million (paid in cash and newly issued Vaisala Series A shares equivalent to €9 M), with an additional cash earn-out of up to USD 60 million tied to Atmo performance and key-employee retention through 2028. Atmo had USD 2 M in 2025 net sales and over USD 6 M in contracted 2026 revenue but is not yet EBIT-profitable. Twenty US-based professionals, including Atmo’s founders, joined Vaisala upon close. Vaisala plans to integrate Atmo’s AI forecast models with its global sensor and weather observation network used by meteorological agencies in more than 150 countries, accelerating its AI-transformation-of-meteorology strategy.

items.title: Masdar Prices USD 600 M Blue Bond on London Stock Exchange for European Renewable Expansion (Offshore Wind, Solar, Green Hydrogen); Part of USD 6 B Debt Plan
items.body_html: Abu Dhabi’s state-backed Masdar priced a USD 600 million five-year blue bond on the London Stock Exchange on October 27, the latest tranche in a USD 6 billion debt-raising programme. Proceeds are earmarked for offshore wind projects in the UK, Germany and Greece, alongside solar and green hydrogen developments. Masdar — jointly owned by ADNOC, Mubadala and TAQA — targets 100 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2030. The bond was reportedly oversubscribed. Blue bonds link debt proceeds to ocean or water-related sustainable projects.

items.title: Peak Energy Closes USD 108 M Series B for Sodium-Ion Battery Scale-Up; General Motors Ventures, LG Technology Ventures & Eclipse Lead
items.body_html: US sodium-ion battery developer Peak Energy closed a USD 108 million Series B round led by General Motors Ventures, alongside LG Technology Ventures and Eclipse, reported around October 21. Sodium-ion chemistry eliminates lithium, cobalt and nickel — using lower-cost, geographically diversified materials — positioning Peak Energy against lithium iron phosphate in the stationary grid storage market. GM Ventures’ participation signals automotive OEM interest in non-lithium battery supply chains. Proceeds are earmarked for US manufacturing scale-up to serve utility and commercial storage customers.

items.title: Marsh, Oka & CarbonPool Place First Reversal Insurance Policy Under Verra’s Carbon Durability Pilot for Developer Invert — Insured Alternative to Buffer Pool Contributions
items.body_html: Global insurance broker Marsh and carbon project developer Invert Inc. announced October 27 the placement of the first reversal insurance policy under Verra’s Durability Pilot programme, underwritten through insurers sourced by Oka and CarbonPool. The policy provides a regulated, insured alternative to the traditional buffer pool contribution used by forest carbon projects to cover reversal risk from wildfire, disease or illegal logging. Qualifying projects under Verra’s Verified Carbon Standard can now purchase reversal insurance to replace or supplement buffer credits, potentially unlocking higher-quality tradeable credits at scale. The structure is regarded as a landmark for improving integrity and liquidity in the voluntary carbon market.
